use: a biology process, from a class handout
request: Use this handout from our health class to make a short on how vaccines train the immune system.

material.name: handout.txt
material.text: A vaccine contains a harmless piece of a germ (an antigen), or instructions to make one. Among millions of B cells, only the few whose receptors fit that antigen are activated. They multiply and make antibodies. Some become long-lived memory cells. If the real germ arrives later, memory cells respond within days instead of the one to two weeks a first response takes.

topic: How a vaccine trains the immune system
intent: Students in a health class need the basic mechanism.
goal: The viewer knows a vaccine shows a harmless piece, the matching B cells multiply, and memory cells make the next response fast.
promise: Training for a fight before the fight.
arc: A harmless piece, many B cells and the few that fit it, memory cells left waiting, then a fast strike.

events.text: A vaccine shows your immune system a harmless piece of a germ.
events.knows: A vaccine is a harmless piece.
events.waiting: What does the body do with it?

events.text: Among your B cells, the few whose shape fits that piece start multiplying and making antibodies.
events.knows: Only the matching B cells multiply and make antibodies.
events.look: the few matching B cells among many, multiplying

events.text: Some of them stay behind as memory cells.

events.text: So when the real germ shows up, the matching cells are already waiting, and they strike in days, not weeks.
